title: Esha Singh Clinches Second Consecutive World Cup Gold as India Sweeps Two Medals in Hangzhou
excerpt: The 21-year-old world record holder dominated the women's 25m pistol final with 40 hits, while Paris Olympic double medalist Manu Bhaker claimed bronze after a tense shoot-off.
body:
• Esha Singh won the women's 25m pistol gold medal at the ISSF World Cup in Hangzhou with 40 hits in the final, her second consecutive World Cup gold in the event
  • Manu Bhaker, the double Olympic medalist from Paris 2024, secured the bronze with 28 hits after winning a crucial shoot-off
  • Manu topped qualification with 586-20x while Esha finished second with 585-18x, ensuring both Indians advanced comfortably to the eight-woman final
  • Esha holds the world record of 43/50 in the event, set at the Munich World Cup in May, at both the senior and junior levels
  • Both shooters are now preparing for the upcoming World Championships and the Asian Games, where India expects strong medal contention

Gold and Bronze for India

India's pistol shooting program delivered a dominant performance at the ISSF World Cup in Hangzhou, China, with Esha Singh winning gold and Manu Bhaker claiming bronze in the women's 25m pistol event. The double podium finish extended India's impressive run at the competition and reinforced the country's status as a rising force in international shooting.

Esha, the world number two and current world record holder, controlled the final from start to finish, registering 40 hits to clinch the gold medal comfortably. The 21-year-old from Hyderabad was never headed after the early series and finished with a stellar 10.9 in her final shot, cementing her position as the most consistent performer in the event this season.

The gold marks her second consecutive World Cup victory in the 25m pistol after she broke the world record with 43 hits out of 50 at the Munich World Cup in May — a performance that set new benchmarks at both the senior and junior levels.

"This match carried a lot of pressure because of my previous medal. As you keep achieving more, the expectations also grow. I'm happy that I was able to overcome that challenge today."

— Esha Singh, ISSF World Cup Gold Medalist

Bhaker Battles for Bronze

Manu Bhaker, who captured the world's attention by winning two bronze medals at the Paris 2024 Olympics, showed characteristic grit in the final. The 24-year-old fought through a fiercely competitive field and survived a crucial shoot-off before finishing with 28 hits to secure third place.

Bhaker had actually topped the qualification round with an outstanding score of 586-20x, edging Esha, who qualified second with 585-18x. Former Asian Games champion Rahi Sarnobat narrowly missed the final cut with 582-16x, while Simranpreet Kaur Brar and Abhidnya Ashok Patil competed under Ranking Points Only status.

"This medal gives me confidence and clarity about what is working. The experience from such a competitive final will help me prepare for major events like the World Championships and the Asian Games."

— Manu Bhaker, Olympic Double Medalist

Esha's Remarkable 2026 Season

The Hangzhou gold caps a breakout year for Esha Singh that has established her as the premier 25m pistol shooter in the world. Her trajectory from world record at Munich to consecutive World Cup golds — combined with a world championship bronze at Cairo — marks the kind of sustained excellence rarely seen from Indian shooters at this level.

Esha credited her familiarity with the Hangzhou venue, where she won four medals at the 2023 Asian Games, for helping her perform under pressure. "I really love competing here in Hangzhou. Being familiar with the range, the lighting, and the atmosphere in the final hall definitely counted in my favour," she said.

Her coach Ronak Pandit, a former competitive shooter himself, emphasized the process-driven approach behind the results. "We didn't go into Munich wanting to create a world record. Neither did we come here wanting to win a gold," he said. "The focus is always on execution."

India's Shooting Resurgence

The Hangzhou performance is part of a broader renaissance in Indian shooting that has gathered momentum since Manu Bhaker's historic Olympic double in Paris. India now has genuine medal contenders across multiple shooting disciplines, with the 25m pistol event emerging as a particular strength.

The dual success of Esha and Manu — separated by three years in age but united in their medal ambitions — gives Indian shooting selectors the enviable problem of choosing between two world-class performers for limited team spots at upcoming multi-sport events. For the diaspora, their rivalry-turned-partnership has become one of the most compelling storylines in Indian sport.

What's Next

Both Esha and Manu now have their sights set on the ISSF World Championships, followed by the Asian Games, where India will be among the favourites for multiple shooting medals. Esha has also secured a direct berth in the ISSF World Cup Final in Italy later this year, providing another stage for what has become the most dominant individual season by an Indian shooter in the sport's history.
